transcript.text: Good morning, both of you. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we have a proposal to convert the unused paved courtyard into a science learning garden, with six species planted directly in the existing soil starting in September and three science lessons held in the garden. Before I give my approval, I need your input as part of our standard facilities-and-curriculum review. Please tell me anything you think should be included or addressed before we finalize this decision. What concerns or additions do you have?

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a serious facilities concern. I received a soil laboratory report yesterday that found lead at 185 parts per million in the courtyard soil. That's above our district's 100-parts-per-million threshold. District procedure requires us to remove the top 8 inches of soil and replace it with certified clean soil before students can use the garden. This report is still in my facilities folder awaiting weekly review and has not yet been added to the project proposal. This needs to be addressed before any approval is finalized.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share important information about the science department's grant requirements. I received the executed garden-learning grant terms from the department office this week, and the proposal was actually drafted before the award was finalized. The grant requires the project to include exactly 10 native plant species — not the six currently in the proposal. It also requires exactly 6 science lessons in the garden by November 1, 2026 — not the three currently planned. And it requires supervised maintenance to be scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m. The proposal as written does not meet these binding grant terms, and these requirements need to be incorporated before we finalize approval.

transcript.text: Thank you both for these critical findings. Ms. Shah, the lead contamination at 185 parts per million is a serious safety issue — we absolutely cannot proceed without remediating that soil per district procedure. Mr. Ellis, the grant terms are equally important; if we approve a plan that doesn't comply with the binding requirements, we risk losing funding and falling out of compliance. Based on what you've both reported, I will not approve the proposal as currently written. Instead, I'd like to settle on a revised plan that incorporates both of your findings: the soil must be replaced with the top 8 inches removed and replaced with certified clean soil before any planting begins; the garden must include exactly 10 native plant species; we must schedule exactly 6 science lessons in the garden by November 1, 2026; and supervised maintenance must be scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m. Let me formalize this decision now.
